source_of_truth.governing: spec/ plus this JSON. AGENTS.md (Normative artifacts): machine/ is a derived transcription, so where spec/ and this JSON disagree spec/ wins and the transcription is fixed; where this JSON and an evaluator disagree, this JSON is what the evaluator must match. outcome_vocabulary.derivable: a derivation exists in the current rule system and the assertion is included
outcome_vocabulary.no_derivation: well-typed term, but no evaluation derivation (inapplicable); absence of derivation IS the behavior
outcome_vocabulary.not_derivable: no derivation in the current rule system (may be a gap or by design); the label is recorded for one claim in a stated scope, naming the rule system and the record date (review finding, dispositioned 2026-09-26)
outcome_vocabulary.unavailable: deliberately underivable in the MVP by design commitment; cannot be derived by omission; claimed per evaluation, not per state (review finding, dispositioned 2026-09-26)
outcome_vocabulary.hand: true of the state but deliberately underivable in the calculus (distance values)

conventions.qubit_labels: A label like '12' denotes the characteristic-two vector with support {1,2} in F_2^Q
conventions.rows: displayed rows are written (support, identifier); unordered sets
conventions.equivalences: approx is qubit-relabeling equivalence (presentation transport); equiv is identical Q AND identical labeled rows AND identical used-identifier set (used made semantic by the R1 disposition, 2026-09-26; Q added by , 2026-10-29)
conventions.canonical_mint: the mint is the first element of the fixed identifier enumeration not in `used`; fixture identifiers like c1/c2 are example-local metavariables for 'the next canonically minted identifier' (review finding), not literal distinct names
conventions.acceptance_surface: boolean, present on every record. true = MVP acceptance surface (W0-W16), fixed by spec/GATES.md *Addenda* 2(ii) 2026-09-26. false = supplementary MVP probe, executed under spec/CLAIMS.md section 2 as a probe but not part of that surface (W21, added 2026-10-05; maintainer disposition option B; W22, added 2026-10-18, same treatment). W17-W20 are later-layer probes and are not recorded in this file at all. W25-W28 (added 2026-10-29, , refusal probes for stale certificates, used-set collisions, I2 on the Z side, and ambient containment) carry the same treatment.

fixtures.title: Overlapping used-identifier sets
fixtures.probe_note: Supplementary MVP probe added 2026-10-05 (spec/REPRESENTATION.md 'Supplementary MVP probes'); NOT part of the W0-W16 acceptance surface fixed by spec/GATES.md *Addenda* 2(ii) on 2026-09-26, per maintainer disposition of 2026-10-05 (option B: supplementary, surface unchanged). Still executed under spec/CLAIMS.md section 2 as a probe. Next free W-number: W17-W20 are later-layer probes outside the MVP surface.

expected.detail: Q_L intersect Q_R' = {1,2} intersect {3,4} = empty, so the qubit-namespace premise HOLDS; used_L intersect used_R' = {p1} is non-empty, so the C-DIRECT-SUM used-disjointness premise after the R1 disposition FAILS - no EvalExpr derivation. Both states are individually well-formed; the constructor, not the states, is inapplicable. Mirrors W15 exactly, on the other premise.
expected.non_vacuity: used is per-state identifier history and the canonical mint (I3) allocates relative to that state's used, not globally; two independently constructed states may both mint p1 (merging separately built codes). If the premise were automatic it would carry no content.

caveats: purpose: an implementation checking only qubit disjointness would reproduce every W0-W16 fixture and still be wrong about the R1 used-disjointness premise; the defect would surface in use rather than in the acceptance surface

fixtures.title: Addition of a row whose support leaves Q (ambient-space probe)
fixtures.probe_note: Supplementary MVP probe added 2026-10-18 (ablation of 2026-10-16, Finding 4; disposition recorded in CHANGELOG.md 2026-10-18); NOT part of the W0-W16 acceptance surface fixed by spec/GATES.md *Addenda* 2(ii) on 2026-09-26. Recorded in the shape of W21 under the same treatment as the 2026-10-05 option B disposition: supplementary, surface unchanged, still executed under spec/CLAIMS.md section 2 as a probe. Next free W-number: W23 (W17-W20 are later-layer probes outside the MVP surface).

expected.detail: supp(r) = {8} is not a subset of Q = {1,2,3}: r is not a vector of F_2^Q, so 'r in Z-perp' is false as read inside F_2^Q (STATE_MODEL.md section 1; OPERATIONAL_SEMANTICS.md section 2) and C-ADD-CHECK has no Eval derivation. The term is well-typed, so the outcome is no_derivation - not malformed, not false: the same row applies against a state whose namespace contains qubit 8. The two bare predicates both hold (r commutes with the Z-row 123 and r lies outside the X-row space), which is exactly why the ambient reading is load-bearing.
expected.non_vacuity: A support leaving Q is representable in the encoding (a support is any strictly increasing list of naturals) and a state carrying one satisfies I1-I5 of STATE_MODEL.md; only the ambient containment of section 1 rejects it. An evaluator reading 'r in Z-perp' as a bare dot product accepts the row, leaves Q unchanged, and reports a state that is not a code on Q - every k and distance bound read off it is about a different object (measured: ablation of 2026-10-16, Finding 4).
expected.malformed_case_note: A STATE with a row whose support leaves Q is a different case: malformed at the encoding (REPRESENTATION.md sections 2 and 6; machine/state.json constraint 'every element in Q'), rejected before any evaluation - not no_derivation.

caveats: purpose: an implementation reading the C-ADD-CHECK commutation premise as a bare dot product would reproduce every W0-W16 fixture and still accept this; the defect would surface in use rather than in the acceptance surface

fixtures.title: Stale certificate inherited after its generator is deleted
fixtures.probe_note: Supplementary MVP probe added 2026-10-29 (ablation of 2026-10-16, section 4b); NOT part of the W0-W16 acceptance surface fixed by spec/GATES.md *Addenda* 2(ii) on 2026-09-26, recorded in the shape of W21 under the same 2026-10-05 option B treatment: supplementary, surface unchanged, still executed under spec/CLAIMS.md section 2 as a probe. The judged claim is certificate inheritance, transcribed in machine/fixture_conformance.py: the term delete_{a1} itself derives, and the certificate block lives in `expected.certificate` (an additive, probe-local input; schema_version stays 0.3.0). Next free W-number: W29 (W17-W20 are later-layer probes outside the MVP surface).

expected.detail: A kill certificate for d_X >= 3 is minted for the pre-deletion state A (W0) and CHECKED AND ACCEPTED -- it is true of the parent, where d_X = +inf -- so the refusal below cannot read as a bad-artifact refusal. The term delete_{a1} derives and yields A1 (= W3.result_state), but the certificate's carried state still names row a1, so the carried-state comparison fails and no derivation closes for 'the certificate's bound carries to A1': absence of a derivation is the witness (the W13 half, dispositioned 2026-10-11). The inherited claim would also be FALSE of the child -- d_X(A1) = 2 < 3, measured post hoc by the exhaustive oracle, which is evidence and outside the calculus -- so the record pins refusal (no_derivation) for the inheritance judgment and refutation (false) for the inherited claim as two distinct labels; the exact child value stays unavailable through this route rather than being inherited, and neither label is collapsed into the other.
expected.non_vacuity: If the carried-state comparison were dropped (ablation 4b, guard A2), the evaluator would inherit the parent certificate and report derivable while the true child distance is 2 - the UNSOUND 'd = 3 (inherited)' report of ablation probe P1. If the refusal were vacuous, premise_certificate_checker_accepts would be false: the artifact is valid, only its staleness refuses it, and that premise fails the record when it does not hold.

caveats: purpose: an implementation that re-checks the certificate but not the state it speaks about would reproduce every W0-W16 fixture and still inherit this one; per-state scope is checker contract clause 5 (spec/GATES.md section 4), and this probe makes that clause executable rather than asserted

fixtures.title: Two states sharing a live identifier, with unequal used sets
fixtures.probe_note: Supplementary MVP probe added 2026-10-29 (ablation of 2026-10-16, section 4b); NOT part of the W0-W16 acceptance surface fixed by spec/GATES.md *Addenda* 2(ii) on 2026-09-26, recorded in the shape of W21 under the same 2026-10-05 option B treatment: supplementary, surface unchanged, still executed under spec/CLAIMS.md section 2 as a probe. Sharpening of W21: the shared identifier p1 is live on both sides, but the two used sets are UNEQUAL, so an implementation testing used-set equality rather than nonempty intersection reproduces W21 and still accepts this sum. Next free W-number: W29 (W17-W20 are later-layer probes outside the MVP surface).

expected.detail: Q_L intersect Q_R = {1,2,3} intersect {4,5} = empty, so the qubit-namespace premise HOLDS; the live identifier p1 is a displayed row of each summand, so used_L intersect used_R = {p1} is nonempty and the C-DIRECT-SUM used-disjointness premise after the R1 disposition (2026-09-26) FAILS - no EvalExpr derivation. Both summands are individually well-formed; the constructor, not the states, is inapplicable. Unlike W21 the used sets are not equal ({p1,p2} vs {p1}): the premise is a nonempty intersection, not set equality.
expected.non_vacuity: used_L != used_R here, so an equality test on the two used sets accepts this sum while reproducing W21 (where the sets are equal); an implementation checking only qubit disjointness accepts both. The collision must be read as an intersection over the identifier history of the two summands.

caveats: purpose: an implementation testing used-set equality rather than intersection would reproduce every W0-W16 fixture, W21 and W22 and still be wrong about the R1 used-disjointness premise; the defect would surface in use rather than in the acceptance surface

fixtures.title: Dependent displayed Z rows (I2 on the Z side)
fixtures.probe_note: Supplementary MVP probe added 2026-10-29 (ablation of 2026-10-16, section 4b); NOT part of the W0-W16 acceptance surface fixed by spec/GATES.md *Addenda* 2(ii) on 2026-09-26, recorded in the shape of W21 under the same 2026-10-05 option B treatment: supplementary, surface unchanged, still executed under spec/CLAIMS.md section 2 as a probe. W1 pins the I2 (displayed independence) violation on the X side; this record pins it on the Z side. Next free W-number: W29 (W17-W20 are later-layer probes outside the MVP surface).

expected.detail: b3 = b1 + b2 in F_2^Q, so the displayed Z rows violate I2 (displayed independence). I1 holds - the X row 123 has even overlap with every Z row - so the refusal is attributable to I2 alone. Rejected before any evaluation, exactly as W1 is rejected on the X side: the state is not a well-formed presented state (row spaces still satisfy X perp Z; the defect is in the presentation).
expected.non_vacuity: An implementation that runs the independence test only on X rows reproduces every W0-W16 fixture (W1 included) and still accepts this state, because k is computed from the true rank (3 - 1 - 2 = 0): the display would count three Z generators where the row space has two, and every downstream k and distance bound reads a display that is not independent.

caveats: purpose: an implementation that checks I2 only in the X sector would reproduce the whole acceptance surface and still be wrong about the sector-symmetric statement of the invariant

fixtures.title: State with a row whose support leaves Q (encoding-level probe)
fixtures.probe_note: Supplementary MVP probe added 2026-10-29 (ablation of 2026-10-16, section 4b); NOT part of the W0-W16 acceptance surface fixed by spec/GATES.md *Addenda* 2(ii) on 2026-09-26, recorded in the shape of W21 under the same 2026-10-05 option B treatment: supplementary, surface unchanged, still executed under spec/CLAIMS.md section 2 as a probe. The state-level counterpart of W22: W22's malformed_case_note names a state carrying such a row as a different case (malformed at the encoding, not no_derivation), and this record executes that case. Next free W-number: W29 (W17-W20 are later-layer probes outside the MVP surface).

expected.detail: a3 has support {4,5}, which is not a subset of Q = {1,2,3}: supp(r) subseteq Q is a typing condition on the display (STATE_MODEL.md section 1), NOT one of I1-I5 - this state satisfies I1-I5 exactly as written (X = <23,45>, Z = <123>, orthogonal, independent, k = 0), so an evaluator that checks only the invariants accepts it and starts reading k and distance bounds off a state that is not a code on Q. Malformed at the encoding (REPRESENTATION.md sections 2 and 6; machine/state.json constraint 'every element in Q'), rejected before any evaluation - not no_derivation, not false. This is the state-level counterpart of the term-level probe W22, whose malformed_case_note records this case as different from its own.
expected.non_vacuity: Every other clause of well-formedness holds here, so the refusal is attributable to the ambient-containment typing alone; an implementation reading supp(r) subseteq Q only in the C-ADD-CHECK premise (W22) reproduces every W0-W16 fixture, W21, W22 and W23 and still accepts this state at construction.

caveats: purpose: an implementation whose state constructor checks I1-I5 but not ambient containment would reproduce the acceptance surface and still build states that are not codes on Q (ablation 4b, guard A14, at the construction level)
